notes.drawing: Direction A of round 4 (picked by the maintainer over a top view and a front view): the bee from the side, facing right. An oval body (ellipse 144 by 100) with two stripes as vertical chords, a round head (radius 26) in front with one antenna, two wings up (ellipses tilted 22 degrees forwards and 26 back, the back one behind the front one), and a stinger point behind. Parts drawn behind another are cut off where they go under it (no white covers in the line drawing). The round-2 bee from above was dropped because it didn't read as a bee.
notes.bold: No override: at 24 the stripes keep 16 units between them and the body edge, the wings 20 inside and the head 28.
notes.fill: Wings, head, body and stinger solid. The front wing and the body are each ringed by an 8-unit white gap, so the wings and head stay apart from the body and from each other. The stripes are white bars with square ends across the whole body, as bug-beetle-fill cuts its band; the antenna stays a line.
